title: Respiratory paper — Dr Imani, Dr Hasanzadeh and Dr Rastegar (undated)
note: All seven supplied ordered-PDF pages visually checked; Q1–40 are present. Source headings name the three teachers. Handwritten circles/ticks are preserved as supplied answer marks, not authenticated official keys. Printed page footers begin at 3; page fields use actual one-based PDF indices. No exam date is inferred.

questions.prompt: Which of the following increases the volume of the thoracic cage?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Sternocleidomastoid is an accessory inspiratory muscle that elevates the sternum and expands the thorax.

questions.prompt: What is normal alveolar pressure (cmH2O) at the beginning and end of normal inspiration, respectively?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At the no-flow instants before inspiration and at end inspiration, alveolar pressure equals atmospheric pressure (zero gauge pressure). It falls below atmospheric during inspiratory airflow.

questions.prompt: Which of the following increases airway diameter?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Beta2 activation relaxes airway smooth muscle. Histamine and vagal muscarinic activation favor constriction.

questions.prompt: If tidal volume is 600 mL for a transpulmonary-pressure change of 3 cmH2O, what is lung compliance?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Compliance is ΔV/ΔP=600/3=200 mL/cmH2O.

questions.prompt: What is expiratory reserve volume?
options: Air remaining after the most forceful expiration
The maximum air expelled after first filling the lungs maximally
Air remaining at the end of normal expiration
The extra air expired by deep exhalation
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: ERV is the additional air that can be expired after an ordinary tidal expiration. The other options describe residual volume, vital capacity and functional residual capacity.

questions.prompt: Which lung zone has continuous blood flow?
options: Zone I at the top of the upright lung
Zone II at the top of the upright lung
Zone III at the bottom of the upright lung
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In zone III, both arterial and venous pressures exceed alveolar pressure throughout the cardiac cycle, permitting continuous flow.

questions.prompt: Under normal conditions, what are alveolar and systemic arterial O2 pressures, respectively?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The conventional sea-level reference values are about 104 mmHg in alveoli and 95 mmHg in systemic arterial blood after admixture.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes hypoxia-induced pulmonary vasoconstriction?
options: Alveolar PO2 below 60 mmHg increases pulmonary capillary blood flow
Alveolar PO2 below 73 mmHg decreases pulmonary capillary blood flow
Alveolar PO2 below 104 mmHg decreases pulmonary capillary blood flow
Alveolar PO2 below 73 mmHg increases pulmonary capillary blood flow
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Local alveolar hypoxia constricts nearby pulmonary vessels and diverts flow away. The supplied B uses the older approximate 73-mmHg teaching threshold; this is not a sharp universal physiological cutoff.

questions.prompt: What happens to O2 diffusion rate when respiratory-membrane surface area is halved?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: By Fick's law, diffusion rate is directly proportional to exchange area when other variables remain constant.

questions.prompt: Which respiratory center can generate the inspiratory ramp signal?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The classic teaching model assigns the graded inspiratory ramp to DRG inspiratory activity. This should not be confused with claiming that DRG alone generates respiratory rhythm.

questions.prompt: What is the primary direct stimulus of neurons in the chemosensitive area?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Local H+ is the direct chemical stimulus. CO2 acts substantially through the H+ it generates after entering brain fluid.

questions.prompt: Which ion has a higher concentration in red blood cells of venous than arterial blood?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Chloride is the source's intended chloride-shift answer, but the stem asks broadly about all listed intracellular ion concentrations. Venous acid-base changes can also raise H+ and alter bicarbonate, so the supplied chloride mark does not establish a unique answer.

questions.prompt: Which condition causes a physiological shunt?
options: V/Q falls to 0.6 at the top of the upright lung
Pulmonary venous blood mixes with bronchial venous blood
V/Q rises to 2.5 at the bottom of the upright lung
V/Q falls to 0.6 at the bottom of the upright lung
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The scan marks C, which represents a high-V/Q/dead-space tendency and is not correct for shunt. Both B (anatomical venous admixture) and D (basal low-V/Q shunt-like flow) contribute to physiological shunt; the broadly worded A also describes low V/Q if imposed at the apex. No unique corrected letter is assigned.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the oxygen utilization coefficient is correct?
options: It increases only twofold during heavy exercise
It can triple during heavy exercise
It decreases when body metabolism increases
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The conventional resting extraction fraction is about 25%, and heavy exercise can raise it to about 75% or more. Thus a threefold increase is possible; it is not restricted to exactly that value.

questions.prompt: Which factor increases lung compliance?
options: More elastin and collagen in lung parenchyma
Removal of surfactant from alveolar lining fluid
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Lower surface tension reduces elastic recoil and the pressure required for a given volume change.

questions.prompt: An increase in which factor increases hemoglobin's oxygen affinity?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increasing pH shifts the dissociation curve left; higher temperature, CO2 and BPG shift it right.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT part of the respiratory membrane?
options: A fluid and surfactant layer covering the alveolar luminal surface
Basement membranes of endothelial and alveolar cells
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The thin alveolar-capillary interface includes epithelial and endothelial layers and their basal laminae, not a surrounding smooth-muscle layer.

questions.prompt: If O2 diffusing capacity is 12 mL/min/mmHg, approximately what is CO2 diffusing capacity?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Using the conventional roughly twentyfold CO2-to-O2 diffusivity comparison gives 12×20=240 mL/min/mmHg.

questions.prompt: Which events occur during normal inspiration?
options: Phrenic nerves are inhibited, pleural pressure falls, alveolar pressure rises
Phrenic nerves are activated, pleural pressure falls, alveolar pressure falls
Phrenic nerves are activated, pleural pressure rises, alveolar pressure rises
The diaphragm contracts, pleural pressure rises, alveolar pressure falls
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Phrenic activation contracts the diaphragm. Expanding the thorax lowers pleural pressure and transiently lowers alveolar pressure during airflow.

questions.prompt: Which statement about pulmonary surfactant is correct?
options: Thyroid hormone promotes an increase in surfactant
It is produced by type I alveolar cells
Most of its composition is protein
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Thyroid hormone promotes fetal lung maturation and surfactant-related synthesis/release. Surfactant is predominantly lipid and is secreted by type II cells. Primary experimental support is cited; this is a physiology fact, not a treatment recommendation.

questions.prompt: Which factor has no effect on the distribution of pulmonary blood flow among lung zones?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: C is the intended answer within the simplified West-zone comparison: gravity, exercise and alveolar pressure directly determine the vascular pressure relationships. Surface tension can affect alveolar mechanics indirectly, so 'no effect' must not be generalized outside this model.

questions.prompt: Which respiratory center provides signals to accessory inspiratory muscles during deep inspiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The classic model recruits ventral respiratory neurons for stronger inspiratory as well as expiratory activity during heavy ventilation.

questions.prompt: Which structure is in the vestibule of the nasal cavity?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The skin-lined vestibule contains coarse vibrissae that filter larger particles.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is innervated by the recurrent laryngeal nerve?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: A is a supplied and valid answer, but B also receives recurrent-laryngeal motor contributions. Human dissection and intraoperative electromyography support this (PMIDs 23515953 and 10334217). Without an 'intrinsic laryngeal muscle' restriction the item has overlapping correct options.

questions.prompt: Where is Galen's anastomosis located?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: D is the best regional choice: the communicating internal/recurrent laryngeal branches lie beneath the posterior laryngopharyngeal/piriform mucosa. The anastomosis is a nerve communication, not a structure inside the laryngeal ventricle, saccule or glottic opening.

questions.prompt: What forms the superior free border of the conus elasticus?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The thickened superior free margin of the conus elasticus forms the vocal ligament. The circled source answer is C.

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies laryngeal mucosa below the vocal folds?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: A and B are overlapping names: the recurrent laryngeal nerve continues into the larynx as the inferior laryngeal nerve and supplies infraglottic sensation. The source circle selects A, but a single-letter grade would incorrectly reject B.

questions.prompt: At which rib is the inferior lung border in the midclavicular line?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The lung margin is approximately rib 6; the pleural reflection is around rib 8 in the same line.

questions.prompt: Which artery is a branch of the maxillary artery?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The sphenopalatine artery is the terminal maxillary branch. Anterior ethmoidal arises from ophthalmic, and ascending palatine/superior labial arise from facial.

questions.prompt: The right bronchial artery is a branch of which artery?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: A matches the usual course-text pattern: the right bronchial artery arises with/from the third posterior intercostal artery. Bronchial arterial origins vary, including direct aortic origins; the supplied answer is a typical pattern rather than an invariant rule. Source 'bronchiolar artery' is normalized to bronchial artery.

questions.prompt: Where is the suprapleural (Sibson's) membrane attached?
options: Between the first rib and clavicle
Between the first rib and transverse process of C7
On the medial aspect of the lung apex
On the anterior aspect of the lung apex
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Sibson's fascia spans the first rib and C7 transverse process over the cervical pleura.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct?
options: The left main bronchus is longer than the right
The left main bronchus is more vertical than the right
The left main bronchus is wider than the right
The left main bronchus has three lobar bronchi
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The left main bronchus is longer, narrower and more oblique; it divides into two lobar bronchi.

questions.prompt: Which part of the pleura is innervated by the phrenic nerve?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Mediastinal and central diaphragmatic parietal pleura receive phrenic sensory supply.

questions.prompt: Which structure does NOT distinguish bronchi from bronchioles?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: A is valid if the option refers to the presence of epithelial tissue: both have an epithelial lining, and larger bronchioles can overlap in epithelial type with bronchi. It does not mean every bronchus and bronchiole has identical epithelium. Cartilage and glands are absent from bronchioles; club cells characterize distal bronchiolar epithelium.

questions.prompt: Which cells are NOT among the standard cell populations of respiratory epithelium?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Sustentacular supporting cells are the named cell population of olfactory epithelium; the other options are standard respiratory-epithelial populations.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the histological structure of the trachea is correct?
options: All epithelial cells have basophilic granules
C-shaped cartilage is covered by periosteum
Seromucous glands in the lamina propria produce mucus
Hyaline C-shaped cartilage is the outermost layer
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The supplied circle is C, but the usual layer-specific description places tracheal seromucous glands in the submucosa. The lamina-propria/submucosa boundary is not consistently separated in all descriptions, so C cannot be silently corrected. A is false, cartilage has perichondrium rather than periosteum, and adventitia is external to cartilage. Held ungraded pending clarification of the intended layer convention.

questions.prompt: Where are Bowman's glands found?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The source marks C, correctly suggesting the olfactory region but naming the wrong compartment: Bowman's glands are in the lamina propria beneath olfactory epithelium. No option states that location, so the source answer is preserved and a literal single-best grade is withheld.

questions.prompt: Which cell forms part of the blood-air barrier?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Type I pneumocyte cytoplasm forms the thin epithelial barrier. Practice options contain an explicit editorial correction: the scan prints 'Pneumococcus Type I/II/III', interpreted as pneumocyte cell names. All four original printed choices are preserved in sourceOptions; the corrected practice wording retains their roman numerals and order but is not a literal source transcription.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the terminal-sac period is true?
options: Bronchi begin forming in this period
Prematurely born fetuses are unable to survive
Capillaries begin to bulge at this period
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: Capillary apposition and bulging against progressively thinner terminal-sac epithelium support a developing blood-air barrier. The item describes developmental capability, not a guaranteed clinical survival threshold.

questions.prompt: Which tissues give rise to respiratory glands and muscles, respectively, in development of the laryngotracheal diverticulum?
options: Mesoderm of the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: Respiratory epithelial glands derive from endoderm; supporting smooth muscle derives from surrounding splanchnic mesoderm. Laryngeal skeletal-muscle development additionally relates to fourth/sixth arch mesenchyme, but D does not give the required gland-and-muscle pairing.

notes: All 40 questions and all 40 supplied marks transcribed; all 7 PDF pages accounted for.
Source Q13 marks C, which is incompatible with physiological shunt; overlapping defensible alternatives prevent assigning one replacement letter.
Unresolved Q13, Q24, Q27, Q36 and Q37 remain key:null.
Explicit editorial repair in Q38: printed 'Pneumococcus' changed to intended 'Pneumocyte'; no new options invented.
SHIP denotes completed transcription and audit, including withheld ambiguous keys.
